title: The IFERROR function: a fallback on error
summary: IFERROR returns the result of a formula, or a fallback value you choose if the result is an error.
intro: `IFERROR` wraps a formula: if it works, it returns its result; if an error such as `#N/A` or `#DIV/0!` appears, it returns the fallback value. Use it to show a clear message, not to hide errors you don't understand.
args: The formula that might give an error.
What to return on an error.
examples: The code is not there, so the message shows instead of `#N/A`.
Dividing by zero returns 0 instead of `#DIV/0!`.

faq.q: Should I put IFERROR in every formula?
faq.a: No, put it where an error is expected, such as a lookup for a value that may not exist, so you don't hide real mistakes.
